source.section: PDF page 19, Table A (MFJ/QSS column, 0-48,000: 24,000) and Tax Calculation Schedule Lines 1-3; PDF pages 19-23, Tax Calculation Schedule Lines 1-10 with Table A, Table B, Tables C-D and Table E; Form CT-1040 Lines 1-6

worked: Federal AGI = wages 45,000.00 = 45,000.00. Federal taxable income = 45,000.00 - 31,500.00 standard deduction = 13,500.00 (given, not tested; federal senior deduction ignored). CT-1040 Line 1 federal AGI 45,000.00; Line 2 additions 0.00 (Schedule 1 Lines 31-37: none apply); Line 3 = 45,000.00. Schedule 1 Line 50 total subtractions = 0.00; CT-1040 Line 4 = 0.00. CT-1040 Line 5 Connecticut AGI = 45,000.00 - 0.00 = 45,000.00. Tax Calculation Schedule Line 1 = 45,000.00; Line 2 Table A: Connecticut AGI 45,000.00 is not more than 48,000.00, exemption 24,000.00; Line 3 taxable income = 45,000.00 - 24,000.00 = 21,000.00. Line 4 Table B (Married Filing Jointly/Qualifying Surviving Spouse schedule) on 21,000.00: 20,000.00 x 0.02 + 1,000.00 x 0.045 = 400.00 + 45.00 = 445.00. Line 5 Table C 0.00 (Connecticut AGI 45,000.00 is not more than 100,500.00); Line 6 Table D 0.00 (not more than 210,000.00); Line 7 = 445.00. Line 8 Table E decimal 0.15 (Connecticut AGI 45,000.00 is in the band more than 41,500.00); Line 9 = 445.00 x 0.15 = 66.75. Line 10 Connecticut income tax = 445.00 - 66.75 = 378.25 (CT-1040 Line 6). No other credits (property tax credit not claimed: no property tax in the inputs, and not modelled). Note: Connecticut AGI under the Table A phase-out start, so the full 24,000 exemption.
